column1: # Example: Streptococcus pneumoniae TIGR4 genes whose transposon mutants changed in abundance during incubation in human saliva, from a genome-wide transposon-sequencing screen.

# Source: Verhagen LM, de Jonge MI, Burghout P, Schraa K, Spagnuolo L, Mennens S, Eleveld MJ, van der Gaast-de Jongh CE, Zomer A, Hermans PWM, Bootsma HJ (2014) Genome-wide identification of genes essential for the survival of Streptococcus pneumoniae in human saliva. PLoS One 9:e89541. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0089541

# Table S1 (pone.0089541.s001.xlsx): all listed genes with a TIGR4 locus tag (140 rows), the authors' own hit list; no further cutoff applied. Licensed CC BY (Creative Commons Attribution License, as stated in the article); values as published.

# Strain-ortholog mapping: D39 (UniProt proteome UP000001452) and TIGR4 (UP000000585) proteins were matched to the R6 index proteins by blastp best hit, keeping hits with at least 95% identity over at least 90% of both sequences; their locus tags are used as index synonyms.

# Columns: gene = TIGR4 locus tag as given; name and product = as published; log2FC = the first log2 fold change column of the table (start versus 37 degrees C with CO2), as published. 100 of 140 listed genes map to the species index.
